1. **Cardiovascular safety of orforglipron versus insulin glargine in adults with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular risk (ACHIEVE-4): a phase 3, event-driven, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority, active comparator trial.**
   Authors: Klara R Klein, Carol Wysham, Katherine R Tuttle, Melanie J Davies, David Cox, Jiaxun Chen, Wen-Shuo Wu, Max Denning, Rong Liu, Lisa Ludwig, Eric R Meskimen
   Journal: Lancet (London, England)
   Publication Date: 2026-10-15
   PMID: 42815506
   Abstract: Orforglipron is an oral, non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. While some peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists have established cardiovascular benefit, the cardiovascular safety of non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonists has not been studied. 2. **Safety of metformin in chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis.**
   Authors: Silvana Patiño-Cardona, Carlos Pascual-Morena, Irene Sequí-Domínguez, Celia Álvarez-Bueno, Héctor Martínez-Martínez, Mar de Miguel-Brox, Susana Priego-Jiménez, Vicente Martínez-Vizcaíno
   Journal: European journal of pharmacology
   Publication Date: 2026-02-05
   PMID: 41548682
   Abstract: Metformin is the mainstay treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but its use in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains controversial because of concerns about lactic acidosis. Previous meta-analyses have been limited by heterogeneous comparator groups and lack of CKD-stage stratification.
   URL: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41548682/

3. **Outcomes of oral antidiabetic drugs in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a nationwide target trial emulation study.**
   Authors: Heejoon Jang, Yeonjin Kim, Yoo Kyoung Lim, Dong Hyeon Lee, Sae Kyung Joo, Bo Kyung Koo, Gi-Ae Kim, Woojoo Lee, Stefano Romeo, Won Kim, Innovative Target Exploration of NAFLD (ITEN) consortium
   Journal: Clinical and molecular hepatology
   Publication Date: 2026-04-24
   PMID: 41492191
   PMC ID: 13129748 (Full text available)
   Abstract: Patients with concurrent type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) face elevated cardiovascular risks. However, optimal oral antidiabetic drug (OAD) selection for this population remains unclear.
